messages:
maria_cs: Escalation from ACME (prod, dedicated pool dp-az1-013). Customer reports sudden throughput degradation starting ~2024-11-20T14:30Z. tokens/sec baseline ~120k -> ~28k. p50 OK but p95 jumped from ~120ms -> ~1.2s. No 5xx yet, but queue depth spiking and tail latency bad. Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CS-8891

kevin_infra: Thanks. Can you paste pool id + model variant + any recent deploys/config rollouts? Also want a short copy of scheduler metrics (queue depth, inflight reqs, batching stats).

maria_cs: Pool: dp-az1-013, model: rwd-open-7b-v1 (quantized q4), dedicated nodes: 4 gpus. No app code deploys reported by customer. We rolled infra change last night (infra PR 5523) that touched scheduler defaults. Paste from recent logs/metrics snapshot: 

```
[2024-11-20T14:29:41Z] queue_depth=312 inflight=8 avg_batch_size=1.6 tokens_per_batch=11200 batching_windows: 2.0ms/50ms 
[2024-11-20T14:30:12Z] queue_depth=420 inflight=6 avg_batch_size=2.1 tokens_per_batch=14200 
[2024-11-20T14:31:05Z] p50=130ms p95=1180ms tokens/sec=28k
[scheduler] max_batch_tokens=16384 max_batch_items=64 batch_timeout_ms=50 continuous_batching=true
```

kevin_infra: Those max_batch_tokens look high relative to observed prompt lengths. If a single long request gets into the batch, it can hold the KV cache until the batch is sent -> head-of-line blocking. Continuous batching + large token cap can increase latency when request size distribution is skewed.

sasha_runtime: Agree. Pattern looks like inefficient batching + queueing. Few large requests are inflating tokens_per_batch and forcing long wait windows because batch_timeout_ms is 50ms and continuous_batching=true. Also the avg_batch_size ~1.6 indicates we are not filling items but packing by tokens. Noisy neighbor theory: one or two customers sending long-context prompts can dominate batch token budget, starving others.

devon_oncall: Autoscaler events look weird too — I see no scale-up during the spike. Autoscaler logs: 

```
[autoscaler] 2024-11-20T14:28:00 evaluate -> desired_replicas=4 current=4 scaling_action=none reason=threshold_not_exceeded(cpu: 0.18, queuesize: 380)
[autoscaler] 2024-11-20T14:33:00 evaluate -> desired_replicas=4 current=4 scaling_action=none reason=metric_window: short_window_bias
```

devon_oncall: Looks like scale logic ignores queue token pressure metric; it uses cpu and a 5m window. If token backlog is short-lived but severe, autoscaler won't react.

qabot: ALERT dp-az1-013 queue_depth > 300 (rule: dedicated-queue-depth-high) :eyes:

kevin_infra: Immediate mitigation suggestions: 
- Reduce max_batch_tokens from 16384 -> 4096 to limit one-request dominance.
- Lower batch_timeout_ms 50 -> 10 (send smaller batches faster).
- Set continuous_batching=false temporarily to prefer fixed windows.
- Enable batch_preempt_threshold=0.8 so big requests don't block small ones.
- Increase min_replicas 2->3 for this pool while we triage.

sasha_runtime: Add a scheduler metric filter: emit tokens_per_request histogram and per-client token footprint; add QoS per-tenant so high-token clients get rate-limited at scheduler. For short term, kevin's changes should reduce head-of-line blocking.

maria_cs: I'm going to apply a canary config to one node in dp-az1-013: lower max_batch_tokens and batch_timeout_ms, set continuous_batching=false. Will post results in ~5m.

kevin_infra: Also capture a deterministic repro: run 40 concurrent clients with mixture: 10% long prompts (~8k tokens), 90% short prompts (~64 tokens). Curl sample for load test: 

```bash
for i in {1..40}; do \
  if (( RANDOM % 10 == 0 )); then body=$(printf "{\"prompt\": \"%s\"}" "$(python3 -c 'print(\"X\"*8000)')"); else body='{"prompt":"short"}'; fi; \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/dedicated/dp-az1-013/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d "$body" &\
 done
```

sasha_runtime: Repro should show tokens/sec drop + p95 spike. Also test with batch_timeout_ms variations. Keep headers to tag tenant id to see QoS effect.

maria_cs: Canary applied at 14:36Z to node-2. Immediate observations: queue_depth dropped from ~420 -> ~90 within 30s, p95 back to ~160ms, tokens/sec climbed to ~95k. Will let it run 10m and then roll to rest if stable. :thumbsup:

devon_oncall: I'll file an incident postmortem template linking infra PR 5523 and the autoscaler metric configuration that ignored short token spikes. Owner for infra PR review: @kevin_infra. Owner for scheduler QoS/long-term fix: @sasha_runtime. Oncall for next 24h: @devon_oncall.

kevin_infra: Follow-ups: 
1) Roll back or adjust PR 5523 defaults to safer values (lower default max_batch_tokens, smaller timeout).
2) Add autoscaler signal derived from queue_tokens (short-window spike) or a max_pending_tokens threshold.
3) Add contingency playbook for dedicated pools (min_replicas bump, instant QoS toggle).

maria_cs: I'll update the customer and attach telemetry screenshots and the mitigation steps. Closing loop once we have a permanent fix.

sasha_runtime: Filing an engineering ticket to add per-tenant token accounting + preemptive batching. Will link CS ticket CS-8891.

maria_cs: Thanks everyone. Monitoring looks stable on canary. Will update in 10m and then proceed to full rollout if green. :eyes:
